## Learning goal

I can describe a need from the user's point of view without naming the solution first.

<figure>
<img src="https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1bQBt0WHBp6ca0RWtQHBHKbfqhzXMc4q4uUOJ8hHxvIQ/export/png?id=1bQBt0WHBp6ca0RWtQHBHKbfqhzXMc4q4uUOJ8hHxvIQ&amp;pageid=p4" alt="Needs and necessities stage of the N.I.C.E. process." style="display:block;max-width:960px;width:100%;margin-inline:auto">
<figcaption>Figure 2. Define what the solution must accomplish before choosing the solution.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Name the user and the change

A useful need statement says who needs help, what should become easier or better, and why it matters.

> **The user needs ___ because ___ while considering ___.**

“We need a laser-cut name tag” already chooses the product. “A new classmate needs to identify who they are speaking with quickly and from a useful distance” keeps the problem open.

## Ask the user

Observe or interview the person affected. Ask what they do now, what gets in the way, and what a successful result would let them do.

[Record the need in the N.I.C.E. Needs Worksheet](https://docs.google.com/document/d/19ObkJz3sYVXwB9VkNUiybXZGZ-ihuGw1FarRj81LtAo/edit).
